verdict.rationale: Groq documents first-party OpenAI-compatibility: swapping in the API key and the `base_url` lets agents and frameworks built on OpenAI client libraries use it. Its llms.txt also lists at least one first-party integration page (JigsawStack), so integration guides exist. However, the evidence shows no named guides for coding agents or for mainstream agent frameworks. Missing for 10: explicit first-party guides for coding agents (e.g., IDE or CLI agents), guides for major agent frameworks, evidence of how broad the integrations catalog is, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can plug the provider into coding agents and agent frameworks through documented, first-party integration guides

citations.quote: To start using Groq with OpenAI's client libraries, pass your Groq API key to the api_key parameter and change the base_url to https://api.groq.com/openai/v1
We designed Groq API to be mostly compatible with OpenAI's client libraries, making it easy to configure your existing applications to run on Groq
